purpose: Teach: 山積み/二日酔い/きもの/スライス/話しかける/掴み/じゃー/鍵盤

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 最近、本気で、絶対、新聞、絶対、山積みに、絶対、なってきたな、ばあさん、絶対、整理、しないとな
lines.en: Lately the newspapers have been piling up something terrible. I should really get Gran to help me sort through them.
lines.style: Gentle opening, voice settling into quiet concern. Slow measured pace. Slight weight on 'piling up.' Trailing thought at the end—not urgent, just the observation of someone noticing time passing.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん。お祖父ちゃん、本気で、絶対、若い頃、絶対、二日酔いで、絶対、休日、絶対、寝てたわよね、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: Mm. You know, I remember when you were younger you'd sleep through the whole holiday with a hangover. Do you remember that?
lines.style: Dry warmth, eyes crinkling. Light tease in the voice—not unkind, familiar. The rhythm of someone calling up a shared memory with a small smile. Slight upward lift on the question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、ばあさん、絶対、きもの、絶対、お祭りで、絶対、着ていたわよな
lines.en: When I was young, you'd wear your kimono to all the festivals. I remember that so clearly.
lines.style: Softer now. Looking back, the voice gentles. Slight catch of affection on 'wear your kimono.' Wistful but not sad—the tone of someone savoring a memory. Slows toward the end.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 最近、本気で、絶対、お肉、絶対、スライス、絶対、簡単に、絶対、買えるようになったわよね、あなた
lines.en: You know, lately it's become so easy to just buy sliced meat from the store. It's not like it used to be.
lines.style: Observational, conversational. A slight tilt of acceptance in the tone. Pace steady, almost musing. The voice of someone noticing how the world has shifted without quite meaning to.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 近所の人、本気で、絶対、話しかけることが、絶対、減ってきたわよね、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、寂しいよな
lines.en: The neighbors don't really talk to me much anymore. It's gotten quieter. I miss that, Gran.
lines.style: Vulnerable underneath the calmness. The words come slower, more deliberately. Honest sadness, not self-pitying—just the simple admission of missing connection. Soft on 'miss that.'

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、私の心、絶対、掴みに来てくれたわよね、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were younger, you came and took my heart, didn't you? I remember that.
lines.style: Tender and sure. Quiet intensity—not dramatic, just the weight of something true. Voice steadies on the important words. Slight upward lilt on the question, inviting her into the memory with him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: じゃー、ばあさん、本気で、絶対、また、絶対、夕食で、絶対、お話しよう
lines.en: Well then, Gran. Let's talk again at dinner, shall we?
lines.style: Warm gentle close. Slight rise in energy, like the voice is reaching toward something gentle and sure. Calm and present. The tone of someone offering a small promise without fanfare.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: 若い頃、本気で、絶対、お祖父ちゃん、絶対、オルガンの鍵盤、絶対、よく、本気で、弾いていたわよね、覚えてる?本気で
lines.en: When you were young, you played the organ so beautifully. You'd play those keys all the time. Do you remember?
lines.style: Soft, wistful opening. Voice lingers tenderly on 'organ,' 'beautifully.' Pace slows as she speaks, as if she's inside the memory. Question at the end is gentle, inviting—not testing, just sharing the recollection.
